title: Telemetry gap led to incorrect tier assignment during abrupt capacity shifts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer-reported production incidents where requests were pinned to an incorrect tier (higher-cost dedicated pools) during a regional capacity event. The problem manifested as sudden escalations to Dedicated despite Hosted capacity being available in another region and model variants being compatible. This ticket captures the investigation, fixes, and rollout plan for a telemetry-driven policy evaluation gap that caused the router to prefer the wrong tier under partial metric visibility.

steps_taken: Captured request-level traces and matched them to policy-evaluation timestamps
Injected metric drop in staging to reproduce router behavior
Instrumented additional metric freshness flags in the evaluation path
Implemented comparator change: missing metrics => 'unknown' not 'zero'; tie-breaker favors model compatibility and lower-cost tier when unknown
Added unit and integration tests to cover partial-visibility scenarios
Canary deploy in eu-west-1 with traffic shadowing for 24 hours
root_cause: During a control-plane policy blob refresh, the router performed policy evaluation against a combination of fresh and stale telemetry. The comparator logic treated absent telemetry as zero utilization, which unintentionally biased selection towards dedicated pools (priority rules weighed absolute numeric values). The tie-breaker logic did not consider metric freshness or an explicit 'unknown' state, so short telemetry gaps led to deterministic but incorrect tier selection.
mitigation: Emergency mitigation applied: router now marks metrics with an explicit freshness flag. If telemetry is missing older than 30s, evaluation treats utilization as 'unknown' and uses compatibility-first tie-breakers favoring hosted model variants or lower-cost tiers. Temporary traffic steering rule was applied to divert high-value customers to a safe hosted fallback until the fix was canaried.
next_steps: Merge PR #6782 and monitor canary (eu-west-1) for 6 hours — SLOs + cost metrics
Roll out to other regions in 2-hour staggered windows if canary stable
Backfill historical traces in the routing-dashboard to identify any customers that received elevated costs during the incident window
Add a post-deploy healthcheck that flags metric freshness regressions in the next incident alerting cycle
Follow-up RFC to formalize metric-freshness semantics in policy evaluation and add e2e tests for control-plane/policy-sync overlap
